title: The popular version. It started as a joke.
description:
It started as a joke. Wikipedia says Peter and Hull intended the book as satire, but it became popular as it seemed to make a serious point about promotion.

The Peter Principle. In a hierarchy, every employee tends to rise to his level of incompetence.

In 2019 economists checked it with sales data. Benson, Li and Shue, in the Quarterly Journal of Economics. The NBER Digest counts more than 1,500 promotions into management and 156 million sales transactions.

The best sellers got promoted. The NBER Digest reports a doubling of sales credits raised the chance of promotion by 14.3 per cent.

Their new teams sold less. A doubling of the new manager pre-promotion sales was associated with a 7.5 per cent decline in the sales of their subordinates, says the NBER Digest.

Consistent with it, not proof of it. The paper says evidence consistent with the Peter Principle. Firms put less weight on sales performance when the management role carries more responsibility.

A satire from 1969 became a finding in 2019.

Sources:
- https://www.nber.org/digest/may18/peter-principle-isnt-just-real-its-costly: read in full. Established that high performing sales representatives are more likely to be promoted into management, that a doubling of sales credits raised promotion probability by 14.3 per cent, that more than 1,500 employees promoted into management and 156 million sales transactions were studied, and that a doubling of the new manager pre-promotion sales was associated with a 7.5 per cent decline in subordinates sales.
- https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:oup:qjecon:v:134:y:2019:i:4:p:2085-2134.: read in full. Established authors Alan Benson, Danielle Li and Kelly Shue, the Quarterly Journal of Economics 2019 volume 134 issue 4 pages 2085 to 2134, the wording evidence consistent with the Peter Principle, and that firms place less weight on sales performance when managerial roles carry more responsibility.
- https://www.nber.org/papers/w24343: read in full. Cross-check of the working paper abstract and its statement that the costs of promoting workers with lower managerial potential are high.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_principle: read in full. Established the 1969 book by Laurence J. Peter and Raymond Hull, the core statement that in a hierarchy every employee tends to rise to his level of incompetence, and that Peter and Hull intended the book as satire.
